stage_status.text: Bounded stages 0–1 rehearsal through a draft question bank. No launcher run id, packet hash, aliases, budget or result invented; neither stage is certified done. No tree, lock, handoff, owner approval or ledger write.

root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: The Abyss makes shelter and dread come from the same Dark. It shields a fugitive ship while hiding terrors close enough to matter; warmth opens clear air, living lamps sustain the colony, and a rare Unveiling turns the country into a moment of wonder before the Dark closes again. Beauty and danger both recur, and a familiar safe routine can become frightening very quickly. Living here means tending light, reading the gusts and the creatures that answer them, gathering food and the fallen grain that becomes fuel, and staying quiet when a searching probe passes. Going deeper offers a greater temptation: salvage a rescue wreck and retrieve an egg and a great bone beside a sleeping, landscape-sized summ whose waking means flight. The haul restores the player's own ship, and raising the summ brings power together with hunger, aggression and growing demands. Rings, exchanges and dreams make a long stay feel increasingly personal, while the Nhaleth remain a fear that nobody can prove. Each of these built promises needs its own demonstration; feature switches and tuning belong to the experience.
root_draft.note: Agent-authored paragraph built around the owner's chosen experience, not his quotation or root approval.

scope.speaker: agent
scope.text: The row is the owner's typed experience, selected by him at the 2026-10-20 sitting. It is the source of protection, close terrors, recurrent beauty, sudden nightmare and fear of staying. It approves that experience, not this new root text.
scope.owner_words_excerpt: The dark is a palpable tide that protects you yet conceals terrors close by. Wonders emerge just as often for moments of transcendent beauty, only to twist into nightmares just as swiftly. You fear staying here too long will find the source of the nightmares themselves.

scope.speaker: agent

contradictions.text: Dynamic cover is built as a saved meter/API. Bounded src C#/XML/Python search found no consuming suppression hook outside Abyss; direct EmpirePursuit source uses static biome shadow. Orbital trade and dynamic raid suppression remain unverified. Do not equate IsCovered=true with actual hiding.

The Dark halo and several donor abilities are explicitly absent from ports; CreatureBehaviors supplies sorter cleaning, not those omitted abilities in the evidence read. Current dark-grown plant fields fix many old glow problems, but some need light and grass has no glower. No current resolved ecological census.

Local suite's scenes audited below. Historical Oct 7 report, Oct 9 deepfire/belt failure and erased Transient references are not available current acceptance logs. No external complete scene runner recovered in bounded read.
Finite elder/ancient stages conflict with continuous troublesome growth requirement. No continuous growth comp or HugeThings Summ-specific growth opt-in located.

Frozen sheet calls darkbeast halo an owner ruling; current port description promises it, but cast bible says halo slate never admitted. Owner's later sheet/source notes must settle build scope without inventing an approval.

Original Lightfall is the place the Dark always clears; later brood biology draft says deepest Dark never lifts there. Current marker places the lair but does not resolve physical contradiction or guarantee a playable descent.

Item says egg may be returned at lip; code refunds within nine cells of original mother's cell, while announcing return to coils. Recover the original option/card scope before asking owner to repeat it.

About/settings header still describe a stub and donor terrain dependence; actual owned defs and mechanics contradict them. Old RUT_Abyss twin references are historical; current campaign patches target RM_Abyss. No mirror edit made.

Local numerical darkness changes Murk and lamp reach; weather sets global sky colours. No spatial air-mask renderer found in this mod. Whether pockets/nearby terrors read as material Dark is a human experience gap, not established by the field arithmetic.
Acoustic banded echoes must harmonise with no clean sensing. Source opts into scanner; precise output and interaction need the scanner's own proof, not a newly invented Abyss targeting system.

failure_modes: F1 — The Dark is a numerical penalty and palette rather than a protective, readable material presence: warm pockets do not feel usable, nearby terrors remain ordinary open-map combat, or hiding changes only an internal meter. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md:7; src/RimMandrake/Abyss/Source/RM_MapComponentDark.cs; src/RimMandrake/Abyss/Source/RM_MapComponentShipCover.cs.

F2 — Beauty and terror never turn into each other in play: the Unveiling is merely brighter weather, ecology is disconnected chores, and the lair is a loot checklist or a fightable boss rather than temptation followed by flight. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md:7; ITEM:ABYSS_LIGHTFALL_BROOD_WRECK_1; src/RimMandrake/Abyss/Source/RM_BroodWakeLogic.cs.

F3 — A long stay becomes arbitrary attrition or repetitive work instead of mounting personal dread: invisible probe detection, fragile lighting, misleading habitat/growth claims or unfair wake timing punish a forty-colonist colony while cryptid certainty destroys the mystery. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md:7; src/RimMandrake/Abyss/Source/RM_AbyssCryptid.cs; src/RimMandrake/Abyss/Source/RM_MapComponentShipCover.cs.

asks.text: Which turn in that little story carries the Abyss for you, and where does the proposed root give the wrong impression?
asks.decision: F1/F2. Your experience sentence joins protection, beauty, terror and the fear of staying. A catalogue of hazards would miss that relationship.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: Protection draws the crew in; repeated beauty makes staying tempting; familiar things turning threatening make departure difficult. I would make that cycle the root's test.
asks.tree_changes: If the protection-to-dread turn leads, organise the root and its main interaction check around refuge becoming exposure. If beauty-to-nightmare leads, make the Unveiling and its aftermath the central interaction. If long familiarity leads, make the existing signs and dreams carry that through-line. All built capabilities remain covered. A different account rewrites the root; silence approves nothing.

asks.text: Which would you watch first to decide whether we understood the Abyss, and what failure there would make the demonstration stop?
asks.decision: F1/F2/F3. There is no owner flagship pick in the evidence read. The most dramatic set piece could hide a weak everyday biome.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: A first: prove that the Dark is both refuge and danger. B and C then show different reasons to stay and to venture deeper.
asks.tree_changes: The chosen scene becomes showcase 1 only after a recorded owner pick. The other scenes retain their own acceptance and interaction checks. A rejection case becomes a core bar if it is decisive; an aesthetic rejection needs a labelled visual exploration before its appearance is bound. Root approval alone is not a flagship choice.

asks.text: What would make you send people out during that opening, and what change would make you call them back?
asks.decision: F1/F2. The built weather can be a brighter interval without creating the tempting, frightening reversal in your sentence. The decision to use it is still undefined.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: Use the opening to read the nearby country or retrieve something previously too risky; retreat when the returning Dark threatens to strand the party. I would let existing dangers change the calculation rather than invent a compulsory attack at every opening.
asks.tree_changes: A useful reconnaissance window needs an outing with an ordinary-sight control and a readable return transition. A resource window needs a worthwhile retrieval and a measured way home. If the opening should itself expose the colony to danger, add that specific existing-threat interaction. No answer authorises global secret revelation or a new attack schedule.

asks.text: While lying low, what ordinary work should the colony still manage, and what activity should force a deliberate risk of being found?
asks.decision: F1/F3. The existing cover needs a believable cost. A map-wide lamp count can make a small outlying workshop decide the fate of the whole ship.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: Food, repairs and careful hauling remain possible around living light; conspicuous activity near the ship or a passing scout forces a choice. I would judge a complete day's work rather than approve four lamps as a magic number.
asks.tree_changes: If concealment is about the ship's immediate surroundings, the leaf needs a bounded ship area and a distant-work control. If it is the whole settlement's signature, keep a map-wide case and require the player to understand why distant activity matters. If particular work is the tell, specify that work and its warning. Existing probes, temporary cover, trade isolation and launch exposure remain obligations.

asks.text: What should a well-run colony do when that happens, and how much of its working day should that response consume?
asks.decision: F2/F3. The built interactions might create an interesting husbandry problem or repeated busywork. The current feed and recovery numbers alone cannot distinguish them.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: Notice one local failure, drive the thieves off or use heat, then resume work; a neglected swarm can threaten the perimeter, but every lamp should not demand constant manual attention.
asks.tree_changes: A quick local intervention needs a readable cause and a recovery scene before the next work cycle. A recurring husbandry task needs sustainable labour at forty-colonist scale. An expedition-level threat needs a distinct exposed-field scene with a meaningful way back. This sets response time and workload acceptance without asking whether the light-thief stays.

asks.text: At that rumble, what can a careful expedition reasonably finish before escape becomes a desperate gamble?
asks.decision: F2. A warning can exist in code yet leave no useful action between hearing it and being attacked. Several workers can add pressure nearly together.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: Stop taking new things, finish securing what is already in hand, and make a dangerous retreat; insisting on the egg as well risks waking her. I would test simultaneous workers and a slow bone hauler.
asks.tree_changes: An immediate-retreat answer needs a warning-to-exit opportunity with a loaded party. Finishing one current task needs that task's duration and concurrent-pressure control. A warning that can already be too late needs a clearly distinct earlier actionable sign. None reveals the numerical threshold, weakens her ruled strength, or asks again whether save/load is acceptable.

asks.text: After a successful haul, what change aboard your own ship would make you say that some of its lost glory has returned?
asks.decision: F2/F3. The repair machinery exists, but restoring generic hit points may be less than the payoff your earlier description intended.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: Recognisably worn fittings become sound again, with enough restored to justify that expedition. I would first demonstrate that using an accepted part restores the ship itself.
asks.tree_changes: If condition repair is the payoff, bind visible damage/condition and actual repair on the correct ship, plus an undamaged control. If named damaged systems must return to service, add those specific restoration effects and tests while preserving the repair-only boundary. If the presentation supplies the missing feeling, explore it with a labelled mock before adding an appearance requirement. Refused loot remains useful in each case.

asks.text: What should become different for a colony that stays a season, compared with travellers who leave after a few nights?
asks.decision: F2/F3. Your last sentence can mean accumulated dread or a changing pattern of consequences. Neither a literal reveal nor an automatic punishment follows from it.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: The signs become harder to dismiss as they attach to familiar places and people; the fear deepens without confirming the Nhaleth or transforming a colonist into one.
asks.tree_changes: If familiarity alone carries it, give the existing signs a long-stay scene and add no escalation clock. If time changes the pattern, specify that change and whether time follows the person or the settlement; use new-arrival and revisit controls. If a costly consequence is needed, define its readable sign and limit before adding it. The no-sighting/no-certain-proof boundary holds throughout.

asks.text: What should make this beast worth taking with you, and what change in the colony's daily life would show that its growing cost is real?
asks.decision: F2/F3. Large health numbers and a hunger modifier can coexist without producing the bane-and-boon story already ruled.
asks.author: Codex Abyss dry run

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; fresh author-independent review not run. No pass or token charge fabricated.

asks.guess: It saves the crew in a fight they could not otherwise survive, then forces real changes to feeding, animal safety and ship space. I would judge the same bonded animal at successive ages.
asks.tree_changes: A combat payoff needs an encounter where its strength changes the outcome, alongside an ordinary-animal control. A transport or work payoff needs that particular useful job instead. Food pressure binds a supply budget; animal safety binds hunting and readable losses; space pressure binds physical accommodation. These choose demonstrations and consequences, never reopen the bone requirement, aggression or continuous growth.
